personality_one_liner: A clean, highly readable, and reassuring medical workspace that balances dense clinical data with calm, patient-friendly interfaces.

spacing.rule: Use generous iOS-native rhythms. Do not cramp data on Doctor dashboard; rely on scrolling and visual grouping. Apply large tap targets (44pt).

do's: Use glass on bottom tab bars.
Use glass on sticky headers over scrolling patient records/appointments.
Apply frosted glass over featured patient update cards.
dont's: Never blur body text or dense form fields.
Avoid heavy blur on the doctor's analytics dashboard to ensure charts remain sharp.

screens.name: RoleSelector
screens.purpose: A welcoming entry screen to separate the Doctor and Patient portals.
screens.layout: Full-bleed background image with vertical gradient scrim (transparent to surfaceInverse). Two large primary 'pill' or 'lg' radius cards at the bottom for 'I am a Doctor' and 'I am a Patient'. High-contrast typography over the dark scrim.

screens.name: DoctorDashboard
screens.purpose: Command center for the doctor: today's schedule, quick status controls, and alerts.

states.loading: Skeleton loading state mimicking the schedule cards and status toggle to avoid layout shift.
states.empty: Illustration of a calendar checkmark with 'No appointments left today.'
states.error: Error banner at the top, retry button below.

screens.layout: Sticky Header with greeting and a prominent 'Doctor Status' segmented control or bottom-sheet trigger (Available, Running Late, etc.). Scrollable list of Appointment Cards containing Patient Name, Time, and Status. Use 'brandTertiary' chips for fast-action filters (Upcoming, Completed, Delayed). Use Medical Blue strictly as an accent to avoid 'generic AI' feel.

screens.name: PatientDashboard
screens.purpose: A reassuring portal for the patient to view live updates, upcoming visits, and access records.

states.empty: Clean medical abstract image with 'No upcoming appointments.'

screens.layout: Top section: Live Doctor Status banner (e.g., 'Dr. Smith is running 15 mins late') inside a glass-morphic or tinted warning container if delayed. Grid of compact cards below for Medical Records, Prescriptions, and Booking. Clear, spacious layout focusing on patient ease-of-use.

screens.name: PatientFeedback
screens.purpose: Post-treatment feedback form triggered 24hrs after visit to capture recovery progress.

states.error: Inline validation errors and top error banner

screens.layout: Full-screen modal/sheet. Large, readable typography for 'How are you feeling?'. A horizontal 1-10 severity slider with dynamic color/icon updates (green to red or smiley to sad). Sticky primary 'Submit Feedback' CTA at the bottom inside KeyboardAvoidingView.

screens.name: DoctorAnalytics
screens.purpose: Data-heavy screen showing follow-up rates, daily counts, and success rates.

states.empty: Empty state illustration with 'Not enough data yet.'

screens.layout: Single-column scroll layout. Use `react-native-chart-kit` for line/bar charts. Place charts inside `surfaceSecondary` cards with `lg` radius. Metrics should use mono-spaced or large numerical typography for contrast and scanability.

instructions_to_main_agent: Implement two separate tab navigators for Doctor and Patient roles.
Use 'expo-linear-gradient' for the background scrim on the Role Selector screen to guarantee text readability.
Ensure the 'Doctor Status' control on the DoctorDashboard is visually distinct and prominent, as it dynamically impacts the Patient's view.
Use 'react-native-chart-kit' for the Doctor Analytics page.
The Patient Feedback severity slider must update state fluidly (use Reanimated if possible for smooth thumb and color transitions).
Fallback to 'surfaceSecondary' for blur on low-end Android devices.
Make sure forms have labels above inputs and submit buttons stick to the bottom via KeyboardAvoidingView.
The 'medical blue' theme is handled specifically here: do not revert to generic indigo. Use the defined 'brandPrimary' (#0073E6) for CTAs and highlighted info.
